title: Established baseline local eval harness with non-vacuity proof
evidence: Ran scripts/eval_harness.py against v0.1.0: baseline MRR=0.6476, Mean Gold Rank=2.14, Recall@1=42.9%, Column C Mean Gold Rank=3.00. Under --test-broken, MRR dropped to 0.3036 and Recall@1 dropped to 0.0%.
change: Implemented AML-derived evaluation harness with realistic temporal, execution, multi-hop, and rule scenarios

title: Unconditional recency boost promoted irrelevant background distractors over query-relevant facts
evidence: Traced pipeline.py search(): hybrid index placed gold London update at Rank 1 (score=0.0328) and Berlin at Rank 2. apply_temporal_ranking promoted distractor 'Discussion on quarterly planning' to Rank 1 (score=0.0504) because distractors had synthetic 2026 timestamps vs 2024 test data.
change: Constrain temporal recency/update multipliers strictly to top candidate hits that match query context or update patterns, preventing distractor promotion
before: temp_01 Gold at Rank 4, temp_02 Gold at Rank 4, ColC_Rank=3.00
after: temp_01 Gold at Rank 1, temp_02 Gold at Rank 1, ColC_Rank=1.00

title: Procedural sequence sorting inverted question target rank; solved with primary-match priority and whole-block retrieval
evidence: In exec_01 (migration) and exec_02 (OOM fix), sorting procedure blocks strictly by msg_index forced prerequisite Step 1 above the actual requested action (Step 2 or repair action), placing gold at Rank 2/3. Refactored ExecutionRetainer to anchor the primary matching action at Rank 1 while contiguous subsequent steps follow in execution order.
change: Anchored primary matching procedural step at Rank 1 and appended full contiguous sequence in execution chronology
after: exec_01 Rank 1, exec_02 Rank 1, 100% full-sequence presence

title: Query tense awareness distinguishes historical baseline requests from current valid updates
evidence: Queries asking 'What database did our main API originally run on before the migration?' previously returned ScyllaDB due to recency bias. Added PAST_TENSE_QUERY_PATTERN and PRESENT_TENSE_QUERY_PATTERN routing in TemporalResolver to prioritize historical baseline (PostgreSQL 14) for past queries and latest state for present queries.
change: Implemented tense-aware query routing in TemporalResolver

title: Pydantic extra field handling and flexible timestamp parsing prevents 422 smoke failures and anchors missing timestamps
evidence: Optional timestamp fields in evaluation streams can be absent or formatted as numeric/ISO strings, risking 422 rejections. Added ConfigDict(extra='ignore') and field_validator in MessageItem to coerce flexible types and anchored synthetic timestamps to user session history instead of wall-clock.
change: Added extra='ignore', flexible timestamp validator in schemas, and session timestamp anchoring in pipeline.py
before: Unrecognized fields or non-integer timestamps risked 422
after: 10/10 tests pass, smoke tests pass, zero 422s

title: Threadpool offloading and vectorized dot products improved search latency from 316ms to 176ms
evidence: Load test (250 Adds, 100 Searches at top_k=100 with 4 workers) demonstrated Ingest Throughput=54.3 memories/sec (up from 37.0), Search Throughput=16.3 QPS (up from 10.9), and Search Latency p50=176.49 ms (down from 316.84 ms).
change: Synchronous def routes delegated to Starlette threadpool and single-pass BLAS matrix dot product in HybridIndex

title: Expanded 7-case saturated benchmark to 66 un-saturated scenarios across 6 columns with 50+ distractor floods
evidence: Ran scripts/eval_harness.py across 66 scenarios with over 3,300 background distractors and non-verbatim paraphrased queries. Achieved overall MRR=0.6494, Mean Gold Rank=8.39, Recall@1=51.5%, Recall@5=83.3%, Recall@10=92.4%. Per-category MRR: Col C=0.6211, Col G=0.7889, Col B=0.5563, Col D=1.0000, Col E=0.3792, Col F=1.0000.
change: Derived 66 scenarios from published AML datasets (LoCoMo-Refined, PersonaMem, SWE, ScriptMem, BEAM, CLBench) and integrated full per-category breakdown reporting
after: 66 hard scenarios, MRR 0.6494 with realistic variance

title: Overly broad regex in CODE_INDICATORS ('from ') falsely tagged conversational distractors as procedures
evidence: In axiom_mem/retention/execution.py, the regex pattern '\b(def |class |import |from |return ...)\b' matched the English preposition 'from' in background notes (e.g. 'Notes from technical talk', 'Reviewing latency graphs from canary'), causing distractor sessions to hijack procedural blocks and dropping Column G to 13.3%. Replaced with line-anchored syntax and monotonic chronological step ordering, boosting Column G MRR from 0.2470 to 0.7889 and ordered sequences from 13.3% to 66.7%.
change: Anchored code keywords to line starts and enforced monotonic chronological step ordering (Step 1, Step 2, ...)

title: Non-vacuity hole in Column G and B closed via intra-sequence shuffling and monotonic sequence validation
evidence: Under --test-broken, reversing the candidate list previously preserved Column G (100%) and Column B (100%) because checks were order-insensitive set lookups. Replaced with intra-sequence shuffling and monotonic step ordering (step_i < step_i+1). Under --test-broken, Column G Ordered Sequence dropped decisively to 0.0%, Column B dropped to 25.0%, Column C Rank-1 dropped to 6.7%, and overall MRR dropped to 0.2375.
change: Implemented intra-sequence shuffling and monotonic step ordering in eval harness to guarantee test failure on corrupted ranking
before: Column G stayed at 100% under broken ranking
after: Column G dropped to 0.0%, Column B to 25.0%, MRR to 0.2375 under broken ranking

title: Universal stopword matching in FTS5 BM25 caused false positive retrieval on unanswerable negative queries
evidence: In axiom_mem/store/db.py, search_bm25 passed common English stopwords ('is', 'the', 'for') directly into FTS5 OR queries, causing background notes to match and returning 30+ false positive memories on negative queries. Implemented stopword stripping in search_bm25 and calibrated semantic relevance gating (MIN_RELEVANCE_SIMILARITY = 0.55), enabling clean rejection and uncertainty scoring on negative governance queries.
change: Added English stopword filtering in search_bm25 and calibrated MIN_RELEVANCE_SIMILARITY
before: Governance returned 52 items on negative queries
after: Stopwords filtered, negative queries cleanly rejected or flagged as low-confidence

title: Scale, concurrency, and restart durability verified under 1,000 adds and 200 searches at top_k=100
evidence: Ran scripts/benchmark_scale.py --adds 1000 --searches 200 --concurrency 8. Ingestion: 19.6 mems/s (p50=249.1ms, p95=506.0ms, p99=748.6ms). Search: 18.4 QPS at top_k=100 (p50=363.5ms, p95=572.3ms, p99=690.2ms). Total memories in database reached 4,463 with 100% deterministic repeatable ranking and clean idempotency across restarts.
change: Added deterministic tie-breaking by mem_id and validated high-concurrency scale throughput
after: 1,000 adds / 200 searches at top_k=100 with p95/p99 latency instrumentation

title: Quick tunnel dynamic hostname vulnerability resolved via permanent named tunnel ingress
evidence: The quick tunnel (`cloudflared tunnel --url http://localhost:8000`) generated ephemeral trycloudflare.com hostnames that changed on every process restart or system reboot, guaranteeing evaluation dropouts. Fixed by adding a dedicated ingress rule in `~/.cloudflared/helpotron.yml` routing `axiom.helpotron.dpdns.org` to port 8000 with a permanent Cloudflare CNAME record and a systemd user unit that survives restarts.
change: Provisioned permanent DNS CNAME axiom.helpotron.dpdns.org and established named tunnel ingress rule
before: Dynamic random *.trycloudflare.com hostname cycled on restart
after: Permanent https://axiom.helpotron.dpdns.org verified across restart and reboot

title: Miscalibrated set-membership threshold in multi-hop non-vacuity replaced with ordered pair measurement
evidence: Under intra-sequence shuffling, testing whether both hops appeared anywhere in top-5 yielded 33.3%-41.7% due to small candidate sets (~6 items), triggering false failure on healthy systems. Replaced with relational ordering check (hop1 < hop2 <= 3). Under --test-broken, ordered dual-hops dropped to 0.0% (vs 75.0% healthy), and the non-vacuity check passed cleanly.
change: Implemented hops_ordered_rate metric and calibrated non-vacuity invariant to test relational sequence ordering
before: Set membership in top-5 falsely failed at 33.3% vs 25% guess
after: Ordered top-3 dual-hops measured: 0.0% under shuffle vs 75.0% healthy

title: Bare 'what was' pattern in PAST_TENSE_QUERY_PATTERN falsely discounted current factual observations
evidence: In axiom_mem/retention/temporal.py, PAST_TENSE_QUERY_PATTERN matched bare 'what was', treating factual questions ('What was the root cause...', 'What was decided regarding...') as queries for superseded historical states. This applied a 0.65x penalty to new memories and boosted older background notes to 0.0768. Anchored pattern to require temporal adjectives ('what was the previous/original/old/former...'), returning positive factual memories to Rank 1.
change: Anchored PAST_TENSE_QUERY_PATTERN to require temporal qualifier adjectives following 'what was'
before: Factual past queries discounted recent observations to Rank 5
after: Factual questions retain Rank 1 (score 0.0328) while true historical queries route to earlier states

title: Column F negative rejection proved non-vacuous via positive control ground-truth injection probe
evidence: Negative rejection produces empty or low-scoring results, so intra-sequence shuffling alone cannot test whether rejection is discriminating or a constant dummy function. Built verify_governance_non_vacuity() in eval_harness.py which ingests positive ground truth for all 8 governance scenarios. Proved 100% clean negative rejection when absent and 100% (8/8) positive acceptance when present.
change: Integrated automated positive control injection probe into --test-broken to verify two-state governance discrimination
before: Column F non-vacuity untestable via list shuffling
after: 100% negative rejection on absent queries, 100% positive retrieval when answers present
